title.en: JANUS Connection Scan — Meta-Registry Common-Mode Failure and Fourth-Order Hidden Node
title.ru: JANUS Connection Scan — общая модовая ошибка Meta Registry и скрытый узел четвёртого порядка

scan_scope: selected historical, symbolic and safety records
scan_method: shared detector and normalization dependency analysis

primary_hidden_node_candidate.name: META_REGISTRY_COMMON_MODE
primary_hidden_node_candidate.definition: A shared upstream epistemic pipeline consisting of source selection, human authorship/context, normalization, detector configuration, classification rules, repository history, and authority policies that can cause multiple apparently independent records to inherit the same bias or error.
primary_hidden_node_candidate.graph_form: SOURCE_A -> MRCM <- SOURCE_B; SOURCE_C -> MRCM <- SOURCE_D
primary_hidden_node_candidate.core_question: Are multiple records independently supporting a connection, or are they multiple projections of one shared registry-generation process?
primary_hidden_node_candidate.why_fourth_order: The hidden node sits above first-order source relationships, second-order structural invariants, and third-order latent mechanisms. It is a property of the evidence-production environment itself.

emergent_invariants.name: REGISTRY_COMMON_MODE
emergent_invariants.description: Several records can appear independent while sharing a common authoring, selection, normalization, detector, classification, or archival pipeline. Such a shared upstream process can make their errors correlated even when their subject matter differs.

emergent_invariants.name: REPOSITORY_COHERENCE_IS_NOT_INDEPENDENT_SUPPORT
emergent_invariants.description: A large number of internally coherent records may constitute one epistemic cluster if they inherit common provenance or common interpretation rules.

emergent_invariants.name: AUTHORITY_PATH_IS_A_LATENT_VARIABLE
emergent_invariants.description: The route by which an object is classified and assigned authority can influence how later readers interpret it. Authority metadata therefore acts as a latent variable in cross-record comparisons.

emergent_invariants.name: DETECTOR_SELF_SAMPLING_RISK
emergent_invariants.description: If the same detection family discovers and later evaluates its own preferred patterns, the observed recurrence may partly measure detector compatibility rather than independent structure in the archive.

emergent_invariants.name: COMMON_ERROR_CAN_SURVIVE_HASHING
emergent_invariants.description: Cryptographic integrity can preserve and strongly authenticate multiple copies of the same mistaken source or classification. Hash agreement therefore does not break common-mode dependence.

connections.machine_observation: The audit and index explicitly define global interpretation boundaries, archive/current-authority distinctions, and non-independence rules that are then reused across many downstream records. The Connection scans themselves inherit the same source pool and interpretive constraints.
connections.pattern_description: The Meta Registry is not merely a passive container. It actively selects, classifies, orders, labels, preserves, and interprets records. This creates a possible common upstream cause for many apparently separate patterns found inside the registry.
connections.why_non_obvious: Connection analysis usually treats archived records as independent nodes. JANUS here elevates the registry-generation process itself into a candidate node and asks whether the graph contains a hidden common parent.
connections.graph_form: SOURCE_A + SOURCE_B + SOURCE_C + SOURCE_D -> META_REGISTRY_PIPELINE -> RECORDED_PATTERN
alternative_explanations: The commonality is partly intentional because one registry defines common evidence discipline.
Many records were generated by the same research program and therefore should not be treated as independent evidence by default.
The shared registry policy may reduce, rather than increase, error by making boundaries explicit.
connections.falsification_route: Construct a source-independence matrix that separates shared authorship, shared detector, shared selection, shared metadata, shared repository, shared timestamping, and shared interpretation. Recompute Connection recurrence after collapsing records that share these upstream dependencies.
connections.notes: This is the current strongest fourth-order candidate.

connections.machine_observation: The same registry-level policy explicitly warns that internal tests are not independent replication and that historical archive presence does not imply current authority.
connections.pattern_description: AIFC is itself evidence-hardened against common causes, but the registry that stores and classifies AIFC remains a higher-level common environment. The anti-common-cause rule therefore needs a second-order application to the archive containing the evidence protocol.
connections.why_non_obvious: A system can successfully defend an experiment against common causes while still presenting multiple internally generated artifacts that share a common registry-level cause.
alternative_explanations: The archive may intentionally be treated as provenance, not as an independent evidence set.
The registry audit already warns against internal replication, making this a discovery of a known boundary rather than a new failure mode.
connections.falsification_route: Perform an external-source challenge in which the same claimed Connection is rebuilt from source artifacts that were not produced, classified, or selected by this registry.

connections.machine_observation: The Connection methodology explicitly favors structural recurrence, latent dependencies, negative-space patterns, and cross-domain bridges; repeated discovery of those structures may partly reflect the detector's feature vocabulary.
connections.pattern_description: JANUS may be excellent at finding the exact class of structures its Connection schema defines, while under-detecting structures represented outside that schema. Repeated hits therefore cannot be interpreted without detector ablations and negative controls.
connections.why_non_obvious: A detector can create a self-confirming archive not by falsifying data, but by deciding in advance which forms of relation are visible.
alternative_explanations: Feature specialization is expected and may be beneficial rather than biasing.
The registry explicitly requires ablation of detection features, so the risk is already anticipated by design.
connections.falsification_route: Run Connection scans with blinded, orthogonal representations and feature ablations; compare discovered-edge distributions to a detector-independent baseline.

connections.machine_observation: Many records can share the same repository owner, research lineage, timestamps, naming conventions, classification logic, and archival workflow even when the concrete claims differ.
connections.pattern_description: Common provenance can generate correlated errors through shared assumptions, common source omissions, common terminology, or repeated interpretation choices. Provenance is therefore not only a trust aid; it is also a dependency edge.
connections.why_non_obvious: Provenance is usually treated as strengthening evidence, while JANUS here treats shared provenance as a possible source of correlation that must be modeled explicitly.
alternative_explanations: Shared provenance may simply reflect organization rather than causal dependence.
Independent physical or external sources may still enter the registry despite common archival metadata.
connections.falsification_route: Replace repository lineage metadata with blind source IDs and evaluate whether the same edge clusters remain.

connections.machine_observation: The strongest recurring warning in the meta-layer is not a positive claim but a repeated denial of independence: internal replay is not independent replication, archive presence is not authority, machine detection is not external validation.
connections.pattern_description: The registry's negative-space topology may itself be the hidden control layer. It repeatedly prevents the graph from creating authority merely through internal recurrence.
connections.why_non_obvious: The absence of an inference edge can be overlooked when reading individual files; across the meta-registry it becomes a systematic graph constraint.
alternative_explanations: These warnings may simply be policy boilerplate repeated across the repository.
A skeptical archive naturally generates many negative inference constraints.
connections.falsification_route: Measure the frequency and placement of forbidden inference edges versus neutral metadata rules and test whether they form a statistically coherent governance layer.

fourth_order_graph.candidate_hidden_path: SOURCE_OBJECTS -> {PROVENANCE, SELECTION, NORMALIZATION, DETECTOR} -> META_REGISTRY -> OBSERVED_PATTERN
fourth_order_graph.critical_prediction: If the apparent connection disappears after removing shared upstream dependencies, the original recurrence was partly a registry common-mode artifact.
fourth_order_graph.counter_prediction: If the connection survives blinded source IDs, independent detector families, external source provenance, and cross-registry replication, support for a genuine cross-object structure increases.

next_scan_strategy.name: COMMON_MODE_DECOMPOSITION
next_scan_strategy.target: Determine which upstream registry dependencies are shared by each candidate connection and estimate how much apparent recurrence survives after dependency-aware collapsing.
steps: Assign every source object a provenance vector: author, origin, external source, date, detector, classifier, repository family, and authority lineage.
Build a dependency graph above the artifact graph.
Collapse records sharing the same upstream dependency and recompute connection recurrence.
Run detector ablations and representation swaps.
Inject synthetic independent null records to measure false bridge rate.
Attempt cross-registry replication outside JANUS Meta Registry.
Preserve both surviving and collapsed connections as separate evidence states.

limitations: This is a meta-registry internal analysis; it does not establish that the registry actually contains a common-mode error.
The candidate hidden node partly arises from explicit architecture, so it may represent intentional common policy rather than a defect.
Shared authorship or shared tooling does not by itself invalidate a connection; it changes the independence claim.
External independent replication remains the strongest route for separating genuine cross-object structure from registry-generated coherence.
canonical_rule: JANUS must treat the evidence-production environment as part of the causal graph. A source can be locally valid and still be globally dependent on the same hidden provenance, selection, detector, or authority process as the sources it appears to corroborate.
